claims.claim: OpenAI safety researcher Juan Felipe Cerón Uribe praised the bill, warning that superintelligence could go “extremely right or extremely wrong” and that “we shouldn’t be playing such games.” Google DeepMind engineer Swante Scholz echoed the concern, stating that the current path of development most likely leads to an existential catastrophe for humanity and that a ban would be a positive change for the foreseeable future.These remarks illustrate that some leading AI developers support the proposed law.
claims.bestSource: Sen. Bernie Sanders unveils bill to ban artificial superintelligence and create Department of AI
claims.evidence: Juan Felipe Cerón Uribe, a researcher in OpenAI’s Safety Systems, said in a statement supporting the bill that “superintelligence could either go extremely right or extremely wrong” and that “we shouldn’t be playing such games.” Swante Scholz, a software engineer at Google DeepMind who said he was not speaking on behalf of his employer, said on the current path of development, the “most likely outcome is an existential catastrophe for humanity.” “A ban on superintelligence development would be a positive change for the foreseeable future,” Scholz said in a statement.
